cards.title: Non-Hermitian Aubry-Andre-Harper Hamiltonian
cards.role: Defines the periodic and open matrices behind Main Figure 1 and Supplement Figure S1.

checks.reason: The operator and boundary matrices are explicit in the main text and supplement.
Direct cosine expansion gives V_-n=V_n*, correcting the extra minus sign printed after main Eq. (4).
At h=0 the onsite potential and hopping matrix are real symmetric.

cards.numerical_form: Build a dense complex tridiagonal matrix and add or omit the two corner hoppings for periodic or open boundaries.

cards.title: Fourier-dual Hatano-Nelson representation
cards.role: Connects imaginary phase to an imaginary gauge field and establishes the localization duality.

checks.reason: Supplement Eqs. (S-4)-(S-8) explicitly print the Fourier transform and the dual matrix.
The discrete Fourier transform maps the two exponential pieces of the cosine to asymmetric nearest-neighbor hopping.
The implementation compares the two finite rational-approximant spectra after sorting.

cards.numerical_form: Construct the dual matrix independently for a small rational approximant and compare eigenvalue sets.

cards.title: Common localization and PT-breaking threshold
cards.role: Fixes the vertical transition line in Main Figure 1 and Supplement Figure S1.

checks.reason: Main Eqs. (6)-(7) and Supplement S.1 explicitly state the common Lyapunov exponent and threshold.
Numerical spectra are real/delocalized below the threshold and complex/localized above it.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate log(2J/V) and check spectral-imaginary and IPR changes on both sides.

cards.title: Determinant winding and its large-L reduction
cards.role: Generates Main Figure 1(d) and proves the transition is topological.

checks.reason: Main Eq. (5) defines the winding and Supplement Eqs. (S-9)-(S-21) derive its two phases.
The transformed determinant is a clockwise circle A exp(-i theta)+D.
Phase unwrapping gives zero below h_c and minus one above h_c.

cards.numerical_form: Use the stable scaled determinant circle and independently unwrap its phase on a theta grid.

cards.title: Inverse participation ratio and edge localization
cards.role: Measures bulk localization and supplies the boundary-state classification for Supplement Figure S1.

checks.reason: The IPR formula is printed below Main Fig. 1 and Supplement S.3 defines the open-boundary calculation.
A uniform normalized vector gives 1/L and a one-site vector gives one.
Every eigenvector is normalized before IPR and boundary weights are evaluated.

cards.numerical_form: Normalize every right eigenvector, compute IPR columnwise, and sum boundary-window probabilities for edge identity.

cards.title: Frequency-domain laser and saturated gain
cards.role: Defines the laser spectra and bandwidth transition in Main Figure 3.

checks.reason: Main Eqs. (8)-(9) and Supplement Eq. (S-31) explicitly define the laser field and gain dynamics.
J=Delta_FM/2 and the AAH threshold J=V0 give Delta_FM=2V0.
The selected stationary mode has zero maximum growth rate to numerical tolerance.

cards.numerical_form: Solve the stationary neutral-growth eigenmode and saturated intensity using all printed physical parameters.
open_questions: The paper omits mode truncation, theta, random seed, integration duration, and the dimensionless transient gain-relaxation setting.

cards.title: Laser spectral bandwidth
cards.role: Turns every independently generated laser spectrum into the plotted width observable.

checks.reason: Main Fig. 3(a) explicitly identifies the plotted object as oscillating laser bandwidth.
A one-mode spectrum has zero width.
Reflecting a spectrum about the central axial mode leaves the width unchanged.

cards.numerical_form: Use the RMS axial-mode displacement from the gain-line center; this is the mode-locking bandwidth convention consistent with Figure 3(a).
open_questions: The paper labels the observable only as oscillating laser bandwidth and does not define its estimator.

cards.title: Exact and first-order etalon transmission
cards.role: Generates both axes of Supplement Figure S2 and validates the physical implementation approximation.

checks.reason: Supplement Eqs. (S-27)-(S-30) explicitly print both transmission expressions and the reflectance.
Both expressions reduce to unit transmission at R=0.
The maximum exact-versus-first-order error is recorded over the plotted four free-spectral ranges.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate the complex exact and approximate functions on normalized frequency in [-2,2].
